messages.content: How is the air quality in Los Angeles right now?

function.name: plant_biomass
function.description: Calculate the biomass of a plant species in a given area. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

species_name.description: The name of the plant species.

area.description: The area of the forest in square kilometers. This is a float type value.

density.description: The density of the plant species in the area. Default is average global density. This is a float type value.

message.content:
I don’t have live access to real‑time weather or pollution feeds, so I can’t tell you the exact AQI (Air Quality Index) for Los Angeles at this moment. However, here’s what you can do: | What you need | Where to check | |---------------|----------------| | **Real‑time AQI** | • [EPA AirNow](https://www.airnow.gov/) – enter “Los Angeles” or your ZIP code.
• [AQICN.org](https://aqicn.org/city/los-angeles/) – shows current levels plus forecasts. | | **Historical trends & long‑term averages** | • EPA’s *National Ambient Air Quality Standards* reports.
• City of L.A.’s Environmental Monitoring System. | | **Health advisories / alerts** | • Local news outlets often post updates when PM2.5 or ozone exceed thresholds. | If you’re planning outdoor activities today, it’s safest to look up the latest AQI on one of those sites—most apps will also give health recommendations based on whether the index falls into “Good,” “Moderate,” “Unhealthy,” etc. Let me know if you'd like help interpreting an AQI reading once you've checked!
message.reasoning: The user asks about current air quality in LA. We don't have real-time data; we can provide general info and suggest checking local sources like AirNow or AQICN. No tool needed.
